## Behaviour changes

- A session at IDGAF now says so once: "IDGAF is on for this session only: your rules, locked rules and protected files stop nothing; each call runs and the audit trail records what would have stopped it. Tools you switched off stay off." In the extension it is a dismissible line above the input, once per chat session; in `cn` one line in the chat or on stderr, naming `--auto` or `--policy` when a flag turned it on. It is a notice, never a question. The audit trail records it as an `idgaf-session` setting change, and a loosening that comes from the environment (`CONTINUOUS_HEADLESS_LEGACY_ALLOW=1`) as a separate `env-loosening` record; that variable's start-up line now says it holds for every headless run while it is set.
- `cn --resume` of a session that ran at IDGAF starts at your configured levels, as before, and now says so in one line: "Resumed at your configured levels: this session ran at IDGAF, and IDGAF is not restored." Pass `--policy idgaf` to turn it on again. Session files written by `cn` record which areas were at IDGAF (`idgafAreas`). In the extension, IDGAF still survives a reload of the chat panel or the extension host within the same editor session.
- In `cn` Plan mode at Questions IDGAF, "Build this plan?" is no longer asked: the turn ends with the plan file saved and Plan mode kept, as the extension's plan card already does. Below IDGAF the question is unchanged.
- Plan edits at Automatic now works as Permissive until a reviewer for plans exists, and its description says so ("In Loop, as Permissive until a plan reviewer exists"). A re-plan that adds more new to-dos than the Plan edits cap (default 5) now waits for you; before, Automatic let any re-plan go on with no cap.
- "Always on" / "Always-on" rules are now called **locked rules** everywhere (the Permissions page badge and Locks card, the Custom policy list, the first-run tip, rule refusals and the docs), so they are not confused with the **Always** list. The `floor:` key in `permissions.yaml` is unchanged. The IDGAF descriptions now say that locked rules are ignored too, which is what IDGAF has done since 2.16.2.
